name: decades
label: DECADES
title: Long-term design
summary: REST trades short-term efficiency for longevity and independent evolution.
quote: “REST is software design on the scale of decades: every detail is intended to promote software longevity and independent evolution. Many of the constraints are directly opposed to short-term efficiency. Unfortunately, people are fairly good at short-term design, and usually awful at long-term design. Most don’t think they need to design past the current release. There are more than a few software methodologies that portray any long-term thinking as wrong-headed, ivory tower design (which it can be if it isn’t motivated by real requirements).”
cite: Roy T. Fielding, comment on “REST APIs must be hypertext-driven”
